newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Intertie back to post-outage levels Sun.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Intertie back to post-outage levels Sun.

text.p: Capacity on power transmission lines linking the Northwest to California will return late Sunday to rates put in place in early August, a source at the Bonneville Power Administration said Thursday.
North-to-south transmissions on the DC (direct current) segment of the Pacific Intertie will be capped at 2,000 megawatts (MW) during heavy-load hours and 2,200 during light-load hours.
South-to-north, the DC line will be limited to 2,858 MW.
Normally, the line has a capacity of 3,200 MW, but concerns about voltage support led to the rate reduction after a massive power outage hit nine western states on August 10.
Currently, the DC line is not operating at all due to annual maintenance work, but this is scheduled to end at 2100 PDT on Sunday.
The AC (alternating current) segment of the Intertie is limited to 3,200 MW north-to-south, compared with its normal capacity of 4,800 MW.
Bonneville, which operates the Northwest portion of the Intertie lines, has said the restrictions are indefinite pending completion of grid system studies.
A Bonneville official said last month the agency's own studies of the voltage support issue would not be completed until November or December.
